brief: A caddy that holds two jerry cans of petrol upright in the boot of my car.

requirements.evidence: I built a ring of 14 two-storey full bases with no floor in two pockets: pocket A is cells (0,0)+(1,0) and pocket B is cells (0,2)+(1,2). Bases (0,1) and (1,1) divide the pockets. Each can stands on the boot floor inside its pocket. The catalog has no bin anywhere near jerry-can size; the largest is about 177×153 mm. There is also no jerry-can prop, so the configurator never checked that a can fits. Each pocket is a two-hex hole about 165 mm across, so a standard 20 L can (about 345×165 mm) is likely too tight. Measure your cans first.
The walls are 2-storey bases, 160 mm tall. They stop the lower part of each can from tipping or sliding. For a tall can that is a low collar, not full support, and nothing holds the top of the can.
The build measures 621 × 915 mm and is 160 mm tall. That fits many boot floors, but I don't know your car, so I can't confirm it fits.

requirements.requirement: Safe for carrying petrol (fuel-resistant material, spill containment, securing in a moving car)
requirements.evidence: The configurator only checks fit and collisions. It knows nothing about fuel resistance, static or fire safety, or crash loads. The pockets have no floor, so nothing catches a spill. The caddy is not tied down to the car.

finish.summary: Two-pocket caddy made of 14 two-storey hex bases (160 mm tall), joined by 17 joint bolts into one body. There are no pieces in cells (0,0),(1,0) and (0,2),(1,2), so each can stands on the boot floor inside a wall of bases. check_build passes with meshClash clear. Can fit was never checked, petrol safety is unmet, and nothing secures the caddy to the car.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
